sentences.zh: 王恭

translations.literal: Wang Gong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong

sentences.zh: 王恭，字孝伯，光祿大夫蘊子，定皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Wang Gong, courtesy name Xiaobo, was son of Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor Wang Su and elder brother of Empress Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong, courtesy Xiaobo, was the son of Wang Su, grand master of brilliant splendor, and elder brother to Empress Ding.

sentences.zh: 少有美譽，清操過人，自負才地高華，恆有宰輔之望。

translations.literal: In youth he enjoyed fine repute; his purity surpassed others; he prided himself on brilliant talent and pedigree and constantly hoped to become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he was praised for icy integrity and eminent pedigree—he meant to reach the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 與王忱齊名友善，慕劉惔之為人。

translations.literal: He shared fame and friendship with Wang Chen and admired Liu Tan’s conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was Wang Chen’s peer and friend and modeled himself on Liu Tan.

sentences.zh: 謝安常曰：「王恭人地可以為將來伯舅。

translations.literal: Xie An often said: “Wang Gong’s person and pedigree may serve someday as royal uncle by marriage.”
translations.idiomatic: Xie An used to say Wang Gong had the breeding of a future imperial uncle.

sentences.zh: 」嘗從其父自會稽至都，忱訪之，見恭所坐六尺簟，忱謂其有餘，因求之。

translations.literal: Once when following his father from Kuaiji to the capital Chen visited him; seeing the six-foot bamboo mat Gong sat on Chen thought he had spare mats and asked for one.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling with his father from Kuaiji to the capital he hosted Wang Chen, who spotted his six-foot bamboo mat, assumed Gong owned extras, and asked for one.

sentences.zh: 恭輒以送焉，遂坐薦上。

translations.literal: Gong immediately gave it away and then sat on a straw mat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong handed it over at once and dropped onto straw.

sentences.zh: 忱聞而大驚，恭曰：「吾平生無長物。

translations.literal: Chen heard this with shock; Gong said: “In my whole life I keep no surplus belongings.”
translations.idiomatic: Chen was stunned; Wang Gong said he owned nothing beyond necessities.

sentences.zh: 」其簡率如此。

translations.literal: His simplicity was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his austerity.

sentences.zh: 起家為佐著作郎，歎曰：「仕宦不為宰相，才志何足以騁！

translations.literal: He first rose as editorial aide and sighed: “If official life does not reach chancellor, how can ambition fully stretch!”
translations.idiomatic: His first post was editorial aide—he swore he would not serve without aiming at the premiership.

sentences.zh: 」因以疾辭。

translations.literal: Therefore he resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: So he quit pleading sickness.

sentences.zh: 俄為秘書丞，轉中書郎，未拜，遭父憂。

translations.literal: Soon he was secretary deputy director, transferred to gentleman of the palace secretariat—before investiture he suffered his father’s death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was deputy secretary director and gentleman of the palace writers—before taking office his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除吏部郎，曆建威將軍。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he was appointed gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel and successively served as General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning closed he joined the Ministry of Personnel and served as general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 太元中，代沈嘉為丹陽尹，遷中書令，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: During the Taiyuan era he replaced Shen Jia as Prefect of Danyang, rose to palace commandant, and concurrently headed the heir’s household.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiyuan he succeeded Shen Jia as Danyang prefect, became palace commandant, and ran the heir’s palace.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝以恭後兄，深相欽重。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, because Gong was elder brother to the empress, deeply esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu favored him as brother of the empress.

sentences.zh: 時陳郡袁悅之以傾巧事會稽王道子，恭言之於帝，遂誅之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Yuezhi of Chen Commandery served Prince Daozi of Kuaiji with crafty favor; Gong spoke of it to the emperor and Yuan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yuezhi curried Prince Daozi’s favor Wang Gong denounced him to the throne and won his execution.

sentences.zh: 道子嘗集朝士，置酒於東府，尚書令謝石因醉為委巷之歌，恭正色曰：「居端右之重，集籓王之第，而肆淫聲，欲令群下何所取則！

translations.literal: Daozi once gathered courtiers for wine at the eastern bureau; Minister Xie Shi, drunk, sang alley songs; Gong sternly said: “You hold the chief minister’s weight and gather at a prince’s mansion yet unleash lewd sounds—what example do you give subordinates!”
translations.idiomatic: At Daozi’s eastern-bureau banquet Xie Shi drunkenly sang low songs; Wang Gong rebuked him for debasing the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 」石深銜之。

translations.literal: Shi deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shi nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 淮陵內史虞珧子妻裴氏有服食之術，常衣黃衣，狀如天師，道子甚悅之，令與賓客談論，時人皆為降節。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Huailing Yu Yaozi’s wife Lady Pei practiced dietetic arts, habitually wore yellow robes like a celestial master—Daozi delighted in her and had her discourse with guests; everyone lowered their tone before her.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yaozi’s wife Lady Pei posed as a Daoist adept in yellow—Daozi paraded her before guests who humored her.

sentences.zh: 恭抗言曰：「未聞宰相之坐有失行婦人。

translations.literal: Gong protested: “I have never heard of a debauched woman seated with a chief minister.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong snapped that no chief minister’s bench should host such a woman.

sentences.zh: 」坐賓莫不反側，道子甚愧之。

translations.literal: Seated guests squirmed; Daozi was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Guests writhed; Daozi flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 其後帝將擢時望以為籓屏，乃以恭為都督兗青冀幽并徐州晉陵諸軍事、平北將軍、兗青二州刺史、假節，鎮京口。

translations.literal: Later the emperor wished to promote leading reputations as bulwarks and therefore appointed Gong area commander over Yan, Qing, Ji, You, Bing, Xu, and Jinling military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Yan and Qing, with credential staff, garrisoning Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Wang Gong regional commander over the northern provinces plus Jinling, pacifier-general of the north, two-Qing inspector, and stationed him at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 初，都督以「北」為號者，累有不祥，故桓沖、王坦之、刁彝之徒不受鎮北之號。

translations.literal: Earlier, commanders who took “north” in their title often met ill fortune, so Huan Chong, Wang Tanzhi, Diao Yi, and others refused the title General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: Because “north” in a title seemed cursed, Huan Chong and others had declined “guard the north” commands.

sentences.zh: 恭表讓軍號，以超受為辭，而實惡其名，於是改號前將軍。

translations.literal: Gong memorialized to decline the army title citing excess merit as excuse while truly loathing the name; the title was therefore changed to General Who Leads the Van.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong asked to drop the title—really fearing the word “north”—and became vanguard general instead.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂入青州，恭遣偏師禦之，失利，降號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui entered Qing Province Gong sent a detached column against him; it failed and his rank was lowered to General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: Against Murong Chui’s Qing invasion he sent a wing that lost; he was demoted to supporting-state general.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，會稽王道子執政，寵昵王國寶，委以機權。

translations.literal: When the emperor died Prince Daozi of Kuaiji held power, doted on Wang Guobao, and entrusted him with leverage.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu died Daozi favored Wang Guobao with real power.

sentences.zh: 恭每正色直言，道子深憚而忿之。

translations.literal: Gong regularly spoke bluntly; Daozi feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong’s blunt truth terrified Daozi.

sentences.zh: 及赴山陵，罷朝，歎曰：「榱棟雖新，便有《黍離》之歎矣。

translations.literal: Attending the imperial tomb he dismissed court and sighed: “The beams are newly painted yet already one sighs the 《Millet》 lament.”
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the mausoleum audience he groaned that fresh timbers already invited the 《Millet》 elegy.

sentences.zh: 」時國寶從弟緒說國寶，因恭入覲相王，伏兵殺之，國寶不許。

translations.literal: At that time Guobao’s cousin Xu urged Guobao to ambush Gong when he entered to salute the prince regent; Guobao refused.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao’s cousin Xu proposed ambushing Wang Gong at audience—Guobao declined.

sentences.zh: 而道子亦欲輯和內外，深布腹心于恭，冀除舊惡。

translations.literal: Yet Daozi also wished to harmonize inside and outside and deeply opened his heart to Gong hoping to erase old grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi still sought reconciliation and poured out sincerity to Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭多不順，每言及時政，輒厲聲色。

translations.literal: Gong mostly refused compliance; whenever policy arose he raised his voice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong rarely obliged—every policy debate turned loud.

sentences.zh: 道子知恭不可和協，王緒之說遂行，於是國難始結。

translations.literal: Daozi knew Gong could not be reconciled; Xu’s plot therefore proceeded—thus state disaster began to knot.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no truce Daozi let Xu’s plot advance—dynastic strife knotted.

sentences.zh: 或勸恭因人朝以兵誅國寶，而庾楷党于國寶，士馬甚盛，恭憚之，不敢發，遂還鎮。

translations.literal: Some urged Gong to purge Guobao with troops when entering court, but Yu Kai sided with Guobao with strong forces—Gong feared him, dared not move, and returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers wanted Wang Gong to kill Guobao in the capital but Yu Kai backed Guobao with troops—Wang Gong flinched and withdrew to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 臨別，謂道子曰：「主上諒闇，塚宰之任，伊周所難，願大王親萬機，納直言，遠鄭聲，放佞人。

translations.literal: Parting he told Daozi: “The sovereign observes mourning silence; the regent’s burden taxes even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—may you, great king, personally handle myriad affairs, accept straight counsel, shun licentious music, and banish flatterers.”
translations.idiomatic: At farewell he lectured Daozi to rule hands-on, heed honest advice, spurn wanton entertainers, and exile sycophants.

sentences.zh: 」辭色甚厲，故國寶等愈懼。

translations.literal: His tone was fierce; therefore Guobao and company grew more frightened.
translations.idiomatic: His thundering tone terrified Guobao’s clique.

sentences.zh: 以恭為安北將軍，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North—he refused.
translations.idiomatic: Courts offered pacifier-north general—he declined.

sentences.zh: 乃謀誅國寶，遣使與殷仲堪、桓玄相結，仲堪偽許之。

translations.literal: He therefore plotted Guobao’s death and sent envoys to Yin Zhongkan and Huan Xuan to ally; Zhongkan pretended agreement.
translations.idiomatic: He planned Guobao’s removal and messaged Yin Zhongkan and Huan Xuan—Zhongkan feigned consent.

sentences.zh: 恭得書，大喜，乃抗表京師曰：「後將軍國寶得以姻戚頻登顯列，不能感恩效力，以報時施，而專寵肆威，將危社稷。

translations.literal: Receiving the letter Gong rejoiced and addressed the capital: “Rear General Guobao through marriage keeps ascending yet cannot repay grace by serving—instead monopolizes favor and intimidation and endangers the altars.
translations.idiomatic: His manifesto charged Rear General Guobao with abusing imperial ties and threatening the state.

sentences.zh: 先帝登遐，夜乃犯闔叩扉，欲矯遺詔。

translations.literal: After the late emperor ascended to the heights Guobao battered palace gates by night seeking to forge a testament.
translations.idiomatic: He accused Guobao of night raids on palace gates to fake a will.

sentences.zh: 賴皇太后聰明，相王神武，故逆謀不果。

translations.literal: Thanks to the empress dowager’s clarity and the prince regent’s martial spirit the plot failed.
translations.idiomatic: Only empress dowager and prince regent foiled the coup.

sentences.zh: 又割東宮見兵以為己府，讒疾二昆甚於仇敵。

translations.literal: He further carved heir-apparent guards into his own bureau and slandered the two elder brothers worse than mortal foes.
translations.idiomatic: He seized heir guards for his staff and slandered imperial brothers viciously.

sentences.zh: 與其從弟緒同黨凶狡，共相扇動。

translations.literal: Together with cousin Xu he formed a vicious faction fanning turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He and cousin Xu formed a cabal stirring unrest.

sentences.zh: 此不忠不義之明白也。

translations.literal: This is manifest disloyalty and injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Their treason was plain.

sentences.zh: 以臣忠誠，必亡身殉國，是以譖臣非一。

translations.literal: Because your servant stays loyal he must risk death for the state—hence endless slander against me.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty invites slander—he pleaded patriotic duty.

sentences.zh: 賴先帝明鑒，浸潤不行。

translations.literal: Thanks to the late emperor’s perspicacity drip-by-drip malice never stuck.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor saw through calumny.

sentences.zh: 昔趙鞅興甲，誅君側之惡，臣雖駑劣，敢忘斯義！

translations.literal: Long ago Zhao Yang raised armor to purge evil beside the throne—though your servant is dull he dares forget that duty!”
translations.idiomatic: He cited Zhao Yang’s purge of court villains as his model.

sentences.zh: 」表至，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived inside and outside mobilized.
translations.idiomatic: The capital armored on news of his edict.

sentences.zh: 國寶及緒惶懼不知所為，用王珣計，請解職。

translations.literal: Guobao and Xu panicked without plan; adopting Wang Xun’s counsel they begged dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao and Xu panicked and sought resignation per Wang Xun’s advice.

sentences.zh: 道子收國寶，賜死，斬緒於市，深謝愆失，恭乃還京口。

translations.literal: Daozi seized Guobao, granted suicide, executed Xu in the marketplace, apologized deeply for faults, and Gong returned to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi executed Guobao, killed Xu publicly, apologized, and Wang Gong returned to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 恭之初抗表也，慮事不捷，乃版前司徒左長史王廞為吳國內史，令起兵於東。

translations.literal: When Gong first issued his manifesto he feared failure and therefore commissioned former senior clerk of the Minister of Education Wang Yin by emergency slate as interior minister of Wu to raise troops in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing failure Wang Gong emergency-appointed Wang Yin Wu interior minister to rise in the east.

sentences.zh: 會國寶死，令廞解軍去職。

translations.literal: When Guobao died he ordered Yin to disband troops and leave office.
translations.idiomatic: After Guobao died Wang Gong told Wang Yin to stand down.

sentences.zh: 廞怒，以兵伐恭。

translations.literal: Yin grew angry and attacked Gong with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin attacked Wang Gong in fury.

sentences.zh: 恭遣劉牢之擊滅之，上疏自貶，詔不許。

translations.literal: Gong sent Liu Laozhi to destroy him and memorialized self-demotion—the edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong sent Liu Laozhi to crush Yin—his self-demotion memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 譙王尚之復說道子以籓伯強盛，宰相權弱，宜多樹置以自衛。

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Qiao again urged Daozi that frontier lords were strong while chief ministers weak—he should plant many posts for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shang warned Daozi that mighty governors dwarfed the ministry—plant allies.

sentences.zh: 道子然之，乃以其司馬王愉為江州刺史，割庾楷豫州四郡使愉督之。

translations.literal: Daozi agreed and appointed his marshal Wang Yu Jiangzhou Inspector, carving four Yu prefectures from Yu Kai’s territory for Yu to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi split four Yu commanderies to new Jiangzhou inspector Wang Yu—stripping Yu Kai.

sentences.zh: 由是楷怒，遣子鴻說恭曰：「尚之兄弟專弄相權，欲假朝威貶削方鎮，懲警前事，勢轉難測。

translations.literal: Kai therefore grew angry and sent his son Hong to tell Gong: “The Shang brothers monopolize ministerial power and wish to use court prestige to trim frontier commanders—learning from past cases the situation grows unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai angrily had his son warn Wang Gong that Daozi’s clique meant to gut the generals.

sentences.zh: 及其議未成，宜早圖之。

translations.literal: Before their plot ripens you should act early.”
translations.idiomatic: Strike before their plan matures.”

sentences.zh: 」恭以為然，復以謀告殷仲堪、桓玄。

translations.literal: Gong agreed and again informed Yin Zhongkan and Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong agreed and told Zhongkan and Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄等從之，推恭為盟主，克期同赴京師。

translations.literal: Xuan and the rest followed; they made Gong alliance leader and set a date to march on the capital together.
translations.idiomatic: They made Wang Gong coalition chief and fixed a joint march on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時內外疑阻，津邏嚴急，仲堪之信因庾楷達之，以斜絹為書，內箭稈中，合鏑漆之，楷送於恭。

translations.literal: At that time inner and outer courts distrusted one another; river patrols were strict; Zhongkan’s letter reached Gong through Yu Kai by writing on bias-cut silk, hiding it inside an arrow shaft, lacquering the fletching—Kai delivered it to Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols were tight so Zhongkan’s message came via silk hidden in an arrow delivered by Yu Kai.

sentences.zh: 恭發書，絹文角戾，不復可識，謂楷為詐。

translations.literal: Opening the letter Gong found the silk warped and unreadable—he assumed Kai deceived him.
translations.idiomatic: The silk smeared illegibly—Wang Gong suspected a hoax.

sentences.zh: 又料仲堪去年已不赴盟，今無動理，乃先期舉兵。

translations.literal: Moreover he judged Zhongkan had skipped last year’s league—now he would not move—therefore Gong raised troops ahead of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhongkan had skipped the prior pact Wang Gong thought he would stall—so he jumped early.

sentences.zh: 司馬劉牢之諫曰：「將軍今動以伯舅之重，執忠貞之節，相王以姬旦之尊，時望所系，昔年已戮寶、緒，送王廞書，是深伏將軍也。

translations.literal: Marshal Liu Laozhi remonstrated: “General, you move with weight as maternal uncle and uphold loyal integrity—the prince regent has Duke of Zhou’s stature and public expectation; last year he executed Guobao and Xu and accepted Wang Yin’s letter—he deeply defers to you.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi warned that Daozi had humbled himself after executing Guobao—no need to rebel.

sentences.zh: 頃所授用，雖非皆允，未為大失。

translations.literal: Recent appointments are not all ideal yet no great fault.
translations.idiomatic: Recent posts were imperfect but tolerable.

sentences.zh: 割庾楷四郡以配王愉，于將軍何損！

translations.literal: Carving four Yu commanderies for Wang Yu—what harm to you, general!”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai lost four counties to Wang Yu—little skin off Wang Gong’s back!”

sentences.zh: 晉陽之師，其可再乎！

translations.literal: Can the Jinyang expedition happen twice!”
translations.idiomatic: Must you repeat the Jinyang coup!”

sentences.zh: 」恭不從，乃上表以封王愉、司馬尚之兄弟為辭。

translations.literal: Gong refused and submitted a memorial citing enfeoffment of Wang Yu and Sima Shang’s brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong ignored him and impeached Wang Yu and the Shang brothers.

sentences.zh: 朝廷使元顯及王珣、謝琰等距之。

translations.literal: The court sent Yuanxian plus Wang Xun and Xie Yan to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Court dispatched Yuanxian, Wang Xun, and Xie Yan against him.

sentences.zh: 恭夢牢之坐其處，旦謂牢之曰：「事克，即以卿為北府。

translations.literal: Gong dreamed Liu Laozhi sat in his seat; at dawn he told Laozhi: “When we succeed you shall hold Beifu.”
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed Liu Laozhi took his seat—next morning promised him Beifu command if they won.

sentences.zh: 」遣牢之率帳下督顏延先據竹裏。

translations.literal: He sent Laozhi leading camp superintendent Yan Xian to seize Zhuli first.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liu Laozhi and Yan Xian to hold Zhuli.

sentences.zh: 元顯使說牢之，啖以重利，牢之乃斬顏延以降。

translations.literal: Yuanxian sent envoys to tempt Laozhi with rich bribes; Laozhi beheaded Yan Xian and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian bribed Liu Laozhi who killed Yan Xian and defected.

sentences.zh: 是日，牢之遣其婿高雅之、子敬宣，因恭曜軍。

translations.literal: That day Laozhi sent son-in-law Gao Yazhi and son Jingxuan to exploit Gong’s exposed camp.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi had Gao Yazhi and Jingxuan raid Wang Gong’s camp.

sentences.zh: 輕騎擊恭。

translations.literal: Light cavalry struck Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Light horse routed Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭敗，將還，雅之已閉城門，恭遂與弟履單騎奔曲阿。

translations.literal: Gong lost and prepared retreat—Yazhi had already barred the city gates—Gong fled toward Qu’a alone with brother Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he fled toward Qu’a with Wang Lu—gates shut behind him.

sentences.zh: 恭久不騎乘，髀生瘡，不復能去。

translations.literal: Long unused to riding sores broke on his thighs—he could not flee farther.
translations.idiomatic: Soft from sedan travel saddle sores crippled him.

sentences.zh: 曲阿人殷確，恭故參軍也，以船載之，藏於葦席之下，將奔桓玄。

translations.literal: Qu’a native Yin Que, Gong’s former aide, ferried him hidden under reed mats toward Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His old aide Yin Que hid him under mats on a boat bound for Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 至長塘湖，遇商人錢強。

translations.literal: At Changtang Lake they met merchant Qian Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Changtang Lake merchant Qian Qiang crossed paths with them.

sentences.zh: 強宿憾於確，以告湖浦尉。

translations.literal: Qiang nursed old hatred toward Que and informed the lake patrol captain.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qiang settled scores by informing the lake warden.

sentences.zh: 尉收之，以送京師。

translations.literal: The captain seized them and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guards arrested Wang Gong for shipment to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 道子聞其將至，欲出與語，面折之，而未之殺也。

translations.literal: Daozi heard they approached and wished to go out and confront him face to face—not yet killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi meant to shame him publicly before execution.

sentences.zh: 時桓玄等已至石頭，懼其有變，即于建康之倪塘斬之。

translations.literal: Because Huan Xuan and others had reached Stone Citadel fearing mishap they executed him immediately at Nitang east of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: With Huan Xuan at Stone fortress Daozi feared coup—Wang Gong died at Nitang.

sentences.zh: 恭五男及弟爽、爽兄子秘書郎和及其党孟璞、張恪等皆殺之。

translations.literal: Gong’s five sons plus brother Shuang, Shuang’s nephew secretary gentleman He, and partisans Meng Pu and Zhang Ke were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His five sons, brother Shuang, nephew He, Meng Pu, Zhang Ke—all killed.

sentences.zh: 恭性抗直。

translations.literal: Gong’s nature was bluntly upright.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong was blunt integrity incarnate.

sentences.zh: 深存節義，讀《左傳》至「奉王命討不庭」，每輟卷而歎。

translations.literal: He deeply treasured integrity; reading the Zuo Commentary to “Executing by royal command those who refuse court,” he often closed the scroll sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Reading 《Zuo》 on loyal punitive expeditions he sighed and shut the book.

sentences.zh: 為性不弘，以暗于機會，自在北府，雖以簡惠為政，然自矜貴，與下殊隔。

translations.literal: His temperament lacked breadth and missed opportunities; though from Beifu he governed with simple kindness he prized himself lofty and kept distance from subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Narrow and politically blind, even ruling Beifu kindly he stayed aloof and arrogant.

sentences.zh: 不閑用兵，尤信佛道，調役百姓，修營佛寺，務在壯麗，士庶怨嗟。

translations.literal: He did not master warfare; he fervently believed in Buddhism and Daoism, corvéeing commoners to build temples pursuing grandeur—gentlemen and commoners groaned.
translations.idiomatic: No soldier, he taxed people for lavish temples—popular resentment boiled.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，猶誦佛經，自理須鬢，神無懼容，謂監刑者曰：「我暗於信人，所以致此，原其本心，豈不忠於社稷！

translations.literal: Facing execution he still chanted sutras, arranged beard and hair, showed no fear, and told the executioner: “I trusted men blindly and reached this—search my heart and was I not loyal to the altars!
translations.idiomatic: At the block he chanted sutras, straightened hair, and insisted his heart stayed loyal.

sentences.zh: 但令百代之下知有王恭耳。

translations.literal: Only let later ages know there was a Wang Gong.”
translations.idiomatic: Let posterity remember Wang Gong.”

sentences.zh: 」家無財帛，唯書籍而已，為識者所傷。

translations.literal: His house held no silk treasure—only books—those who understood mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He died owning books alone—knowing men grieved.

sentences.zh: 恭美姿儀，人多愛悅，或目之云「濯濯如春月柳」。

translations.literal: Gong’s looks were beautiful—many adored him; some compared him to “spring willow washed bright.”
translations.idiomatic: His beauty drew admirers—“lustrous as spring willows.”

sentences.zh: 嘗被鶴氅裘，涉雪而行，孟昶窺見之，歎曰：「此真神仙中人也！

translations.literal: Once wearing crane-feather cloak he walked through snow; Meng Chang peeked and sighed: “Truly an immortal among men!”
translations.idiomatic: In crane cloak crossing snow Meng Chang gasped he looked immortal.

sentences.zh: 」初見執，遇故吏戴耆之為湖孰令，恭私告之曰：「我有庶兒未舉，在乳母家，卿為我送寄桓南郡。

translations.literal: When first seized he met former clerk Dai Zhizhi, magistrate of Hushu; Gong whispered: “I have a bastard son unregistered at his nurse’s—please send him to Colonel Huan of the south.”
translations.idiomatic: Captured he begged Dai Zhizhi to ferry a hidden bastard son to Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 」耆之遂送之于夏口。

translations.literal: Zhizhi therefore delivered him to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhizhi brought the child to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 桓玄撫養之，為立喪庭弔祭焉。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan raised him and erected mourning sheds to lament him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan adopted the boy and mourned Wang Gong formally.

sentences.zh: 及玄執政，上表理恭，詔贈侍中、太保，諡曰忠簡。

translations.literal: When Xuan seized power he memorialized Gong’s innocence—an edict posthumously named him Palace Attendant and grand guardian with posthumous epithet Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan’s regime rehabilitated Wang Gong as palace attendant and grand guardian “Loyal-and-Simple.”

sentences.zh: 爽贈太常，和及子簡並通直散騎郎，殷確散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Shuang was posthumously honored Chamberlain for Ceremonial; He and son Jian received supernumerary gentleman positions; Yin Que became gentleman of palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors rolled down to kin and Yin Que.

sentences.zh: 腰斬湖浦尉及錢強等。

translations.literal: The lake patrol captain and Qian Qiang were halved at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Informant captain and Qian Qiang died by waist-chopping.

sentences.zh: 恭庶子曇亨，義熙中為給事中。

translations.literal: Gong’s bastard Tanheng served as palace aide under Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: Bastard son Tanheng later served as palace aide.

sentences.zh: 庾楷

translations.literal: Yu Kai
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai

sentences.zh: 庾楷，征西將軍亮之孫，會稽內史羲小子也。

translations.literal: Yu Kai was grandson of General Who Conquers the West Yu Liang and youngest son of Interior Minister of Kuaiji Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai descended from Yu Liang and was Yu Xi’s youngest son.

sentences.zh: 初拜侍中，代兄准為西中郎將、豫州刺史、假節，鎮曆陽。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed palace attendant, succeeding elder brother Zhun as General of the Western Gentlemen of the Household, Inspector of Yu Province with credential staff, garrisoning Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He opened his career as palace attendant, replacing brother Yu Zhun as western household general and Yu inspector at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 隆安初，進號左將軍。

translations.literal: In the early Longan era his title advanced to General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Early Longan promoted him to general of the left.

sentences.zh: 時會稽王道子憚王恭、殷仲堪等擅兵，故出王愉為江州，督豫州四郡，以為形援。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Daozi of Kuaiji feared Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan holding armies and therefore sent Wang Yu out as Jiangzhou Inspector supervising four Yu commanderies as strategic support.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi feared Wang Gong and Zhongkan—stationed Wang Yu in Jiangzhou over four Yu counties as backup.

sentences.zh: 楷上疏以江州非險塞之地，而西府北帶寇戎，不應使愉分督，詔不許。

translations.literal: Kai memorialized that Jiangzhou was no choke-point country while the western headquarters fronts northern raiders—Yu should not divide supervision—an edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai protested that Jiangzhou was no fortress and the western wing faced barbarians—Wang Yu should not split authority—the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 時楷懷恨，使子鴻說王恭，以譙王尚之兄弟復握機權，勢過國寶。

translations.literal: At that time Kai harbored resentment and sent his son Hong to persuade Wang Gong that Prince Shang’s brothers again grasped leverage exceeding Guobao’s.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai, bitter, had Yu Hong tell Wang Gong the Shang brothers now outweighed Guobao in power.

sentences.zh: 恭亦素忌尚之。

translations.literal: Gong likewise always envied Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong already resented Shang.

sentences.zh: 遂連謀舉兵。

translations.literal: They therefore jointly plotted to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: They conspired to rebel together.

sentences.zh: 事在恭傳。

translations.literal: The affair appears in Gong’s biography.
translations.idiomatic: Details appear under Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 詔使尚之討楷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shang to campaign against Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Court ordered Sima Shang to attack Yu Kai.

sentences.zh: 楷遣汝南太守段方逆尚之，戰於慈湖，方大敗，被殺，楷奔于桓玄。

translations.literal: Kai sent Administrator of Runan Duan Fang to oppose Shang at Cihu—Fang suffered great defeat, was killed, and Kai fled to Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai sent Duan Fang to Cihu—Fang died routed—and Kai fled to Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 及玄等盟于柴桑，連名上疏自理，詔赦玄等而不赦恭、楷，楷遂依玄，玄用為武昌太守。

translations.literal: When Xuan and allies swore covenant at Chaisang and jointly memorialized self-defense an edict pardoned Xuan’s party but not Gong or Kai—Kai therefore attached to Xuan who employed him as Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaisang covenant edicts spared Xuan’s allies but not Wang Gong or Yu Kai—Kai joined Xuan as Wuchang prefect.

sentences.zh: 楷後懼玄必敗，密遣使結會稽世子元顯：「若朝廷討玄，當為內應。

translations.literal: Later Kai feared Xuan must fail and secretly sent envoys to ally with heir Yuanxian of Kuaiji: “If court attacks Xuan I shall be inner collaborator.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai later feared Xuan would lose and secretly promised Yuanxian to turn coat during a strike on Xuan.

sentences.zh: 」及玄得志，楷以謀泄，為玄所誅。

translations.literal: When Xuan achieved his aims Kai’s plot leaked and Xuan executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuan triumphed Yu Kai’s treachery surfaced and Xuan killed him.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi

sentences.zh: 劉牢之，字道堅，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi, courtesy name Daojian, was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi, courtesy Daojian, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 曾祖羲，以善射事武帝，曆北地、雁門太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xi served Emperor Wu with skilled archery and successively administered Beidi and Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Liu Xi impressed Emperor Wu with archery and governed northern frontier commanderies.

sentences.zh: 父建，有武幹，為征虜將軍。

translations.literal: His father Jian possessed martial talent and served as General Who Conquers the Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: Father Liu Jian was martial—general who conquers the Caitiffs.

sentences.zh: 世以壯勇稱。

translations.literal: For generations they were famed stalwart courage.
translations.idiomatic: The clan was famed for martial grit.

sentences.zh: 牢之面紫赤色，須目驚人，而沈毅多計畫。

translations.literal: Laozhi’s face was purplish red; beard and brows awed others yet he was steady and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi had a purple-red face, startling whiskers, deep calm, and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 太元初，謝玄北鎮廣陵，時苻堅方盛，玄多募勁勇，牢之與東海何謙、琅邪諸葛侃、樂安高衡、東平劉軌、西河田洛及晉陵孫無終等以驍猛應選。

translations.literal: Early in Taiyuan Xie Xuanchong garrisoned Guangling while Fu Jian flourished—Xuan recruited fierce fighters; Laozhi with He Qian of Donghai, Zhuge Kan of Langye, Gao Heng of Le’an, Liu Gui of Dongping, Tian Luo of Xihe, and Sun Wuzhong of Jinling answered selection for valor.
translations.idiomatic: Early Taiyuan Xie Xuan recruited elite troops—Laozhi joined He Qian, Zhuge Kan, and others as shock picks.

sentences.zh: 玄以牢之為參軍，領精銳為前鋒，百戰百勝，號為「北府兵」，敵人畏之。

translations.literal: Xuan appointed Laozhi army adviser leading crack troops as vanguard—hundred battles hundred victories—styled “Beifu troops”—foes feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan made him adviser commanding the storied Beifu vanguard—undefeated and dreaded.

sentences.zh: 及堅將句難南侵，玄率何謙等距之。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian’s general Ju Nan invaded south Xuan led He Qian and others to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Against Fu Jian’s general Ju Nan Xie Xuan marched He Qian and Laozhi.

sentences.zh: 牢之破難輜重於盱眙，獲其運船，遷鷹揚將軍、廣陵相。

translations.literal: Laozhi smashed Nan’s baggage train at Xuyi, captured supply ships, rose General Who Spreads Wings, and became Chancellor of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi smashed Ju Nan’s baggage at Xuyi, seized transports, became spreading-wings general and Guangling governor.

sentences.zh: 時車騎將軍桓衝擊襄陽，宣城內史胡彬率眾向壽陽，以為沖聲援。

translations.literal: At that time chariot-and-cavalry general Huan Chong attacked Xiangyang while Interior Minister of Xuancheng Hu Bin marched toward Shouyang to screen Chong.
translations.idiomatic: While Huan Chong struck Xiangyang Hu Bin advanced on Shouyang in support.

sentences.zh: 牢之領卒二千，為彬後繼。

translations.literal: Laozhi led two thousand men as Bin’s rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi followed with two thousand rear-echelon troops.

sentences.zh: 淮肥之役，苻堅遣其弟融及驍將張蠔攻陷壽陽，謝玄使彬與牢之距之。

translations.literal: During Huai-Fei Fu Jian sent brother Rong and fierce general Zhang Hao to seize Shouyang—Xie Xuan ordered Bin and Laozhi to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: At Fei River Fu Rong and Zhang Hao took Shouyang—Xuan ordered Bin and Laozhi forward.

sentences.zh: 師次硤石，不敢進。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xiashi and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: They stalled at Xiashi afraid to advance.

sentences.zh: 堅將梁成又以二萬人屯洛澗，玄遣牢之以精卒五千距之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s general Liang Cheng further camped twenty thousand at Luojian—Xuan dispatched Laozhi with five thousand elites against him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cheng blocked Luojian with twenty thousand—Laozhi took five thousand elites.

sentences.zh: 去賊十里，成阻澗列陣。

translations.literal: Ten li from the enemy Cheng barred the stream and formed ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li out Liang Cheng lined the ford.

sentences.zh: 牢之率參軍劉襲、諸葛求等直進渡水，臨陣斬成及其弟雲，又分兵斷其歸津。

translations.literal: Laozhi led aides Liu Xi and Zhuge Qiu straight across the water, slew Cheng and brother Yun in formation, and detached troops to cut retreat ferries.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi forded, killed Liang Cheng and his brother, severed retreat bridges.

sentences.zh: 賊步騎崩潰，爭赴淮水，殺獲萬餘人，盡收其器械。

translations.literal: Enemy infantry and horse collapsed racing for the Huai—over ten thousand killed or captured—all arms seized.
translations.idiomatic: Fu troops stampeded into the Huai—ten thousand casualties—full baggage taken.

sentences.zh: 堅尋亦大敗，歸長安，餘黨所在屯結。

translations.literal: Fu Jian soon suffered crushing defeat and fled to Chang’an—remnants dug in everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian fled to Chang’an—stragglers holed up widely.

sentences.zh: 牢之進平譙城，使安豐太守戴寶戍之。

translations.literal: Laozhi advanced to pacify Qiao city and ordered Administrator of Anfeng Dai Bao to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi cleared Qiao and left Dai Bao garrisoning.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、彭城內史，以功賜爵武岡縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He rose General Who Soars like the Dragon, Interior Minister of Pengcheng, enfeoffed village baron of Wugang with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted dragon-soaring general, Pengcheng prefect, baron of Wugang at five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 牢之進屯鄄城，討諸未服，河南城堡承風歸順者甚眾。

translations.literal: Laozhi advanced camp to Juancheng and subdued holdouts—many Henan fortresses surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Camped at Juancheng he brought unruly Henan castles to heel.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅子丕據鄴，為慕容垂所逼，請降，牢之引兵救之。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian’s son Pi held Ye pressed by Murong Chui Pi sued for surrender—Laozhi marched to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi besieged at Ye begged rescue from Murong Chui—Laozhi marched north.

sentences.zh: 垂聞軍至，出新城北走。

translations.literal: Chui heard the army approached and fled north from New City.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui fled north from New City when Laozhi approached.

sentences.zh: 牢之與沛郡太守田次之追之，行二百里，至五橋澤中，爭趣輜重，稍亂，為垂所擊，牢之敗績，士卒殲焉。

translations.literal: Laozhi with Administrator of Pei Tian Cizhi pursued two hundred li into Five Bridges marsh—troops scrambled for baggage, fell into disorder, and Chui struck—Laozhi suffered crushing defeat—soldiers annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing through Five Bridges marsh greed for baggage broke ranks—Murong Chui routed Laozhi.

sentences.zh: 牢之策馬跳五丈澗，得脫。

translations.literal: Laozhi spurred his horse across a five-zhang stream and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He leapt a five-zhang gully and escaped.

sentences.zh: 會丕救至，因入臨漳，集亡散，兵復少振。

translations.literal: When Pi’s relief arrived he entered Linzhang gathering survivors—troops revived somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi’s reinforcements let him regroup at Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 牢之以軍敗征還。

translations.literal: Laozhi was recalled because of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat summoned him home.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復為龍驤將軍，守淮陰。

translations.literal: Before long he again served General Who Soars like the Dragon guarding Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon restored as dragon-soaring general defending Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 後進戍彭城，復領太守。

translations.literal: Later he advanced garrison to Pengcheng and again headed the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he garrisoned Pengcheng as prefect again.

sentences.zh: 祅賊劉黎僭尊號於皇丘，牢之討滅之。

translations.literal: Sectarian rebel Liu Li declared imperial title at Huangqiu—Laozhi destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Liu Li crowned himself at Huangqiu—Laozhi crushed him.

sentences.zh: 苻堅將張遇遣兵擊破金鄉。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s general Zhang Yu sent troops to smash Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu seized Jinxiang for Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 圍太山太守羊邁，牢之遣參軍向欽之擊走之。

translations.literal: Besieging Taishan Prefect Yang Mai Laozhi sent aide Xiang Qinzhi to drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi relieved Yang Mai’s Taishan siege via Xiang Qinzhi.

sentences.zh: 會慕容垂叛將翟釗救遇，牢之引還。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui’s rebel general Zhai Zhao aided Yu Laozhi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhao reinforced Zhang Yu—Laozhi pulled back.

sentences.zh: 釗還，牢之進平太山，追釗於鄄城，釗走河北，因獲張遇以歸之彭城。

translations.literal: Zhao withdrew; Laozhi advanced to pacify Taishan, chased Zhao to Juancheng—Zhao fled north—thereby capturing Zhang Yu and returning him to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Taishan, chased Zhai Zhao north, captured Zhang Yu for Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 襖賊司馬徽聚黨馬頭山，牢之遣參軍竺朗之討滅之。

translations.literal: Sectarian rebel Sima Hui gathered bandits at Matou Mountain—Laozhi sent aide Zhu Langzhi to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Hui’s Matou bandits fell to Zhu Langzhi.

sentences.zh: 時慕容氏掠廩丘，高平太守徐含遠告急，牢之不能救，坐畏懦免。

translations.literal: When Murong raiders plundered Linqiu Prefect Xu Hanyuan called urgent relief Laozhi failed to save—he was dismissed for cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to relieve Linqiu—cashiered for cowardice.

sentences.zh: 及王恭將討王國寶，引牢之為府司馬，領南彭城內史，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong prepared to attack Wang Guobao he brought Laozhi in as marshal of staff and concurrent interior minister of southern Pengcheng plus General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong named Liu Laozhi army marshal and southern Pengcheng prefect when moving against Guobao.

sentences.zh: 恭使牢之討破王廞，以牢之領晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Gong ordered Laozhi to crush Wang Yin and then placed Laozhi as Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi smashed Wang Yin then became Jinling prefect.

sentences.zh: 恭本以才地陵物，及檄至京師，朝廷戮國寶、王緒，自謂威德已著，雖杖牢之為爪牙，但以行陣武將相遇，禮之甚薄。

translations.literal: Gong originally lorded talent and pedigree over others; once his proclamation reached the capital and court executed Guobao and Wang Xu he assumed awe covered him—though leaning on Laozhi as claws he treated him merely as battlefield soldier with very thin courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After Guobao fell Wang Gong sneered at Liu Laozhi as mere grunt despite relying on him.

sentences.zh: 牢之負其才能，深懷恥恨。

translations.literal: Laozhi bore his abilities with deep shame and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi nursed bitter shame.

sentences.zh: 及恭之後舉，元顯遣廬江太守高素說牢之使叛恭，事成，當即其位號，牢之許焉。

translations.literal: When Gong rose again Yuanxian sent Administrator of Lujiang Gao Su to persuade Laozhi to betray Gong—promising his rank if successful—Laozhi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian’s Gao Su bought Laozhi’s defection with Wang Gong’s command promise.

sentences.zh: 恭參軍何澹之以其謀告恭。

translations.literal: Gong’s aide He Danzhi informed Gong of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: He Danzhi warned Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 牢之與澹之有隙，故恭疑而不納。

translations.literal: Laozhi and Danzhi had friction therefore Gong doubted and rejected the warning.
translations.idiomatic: Feuds let Wang Gong dismiss He Danzhi’s tip.

sentences.zh: 乃置酒請牢之於眾中，拜牢之為兄，精兵利器悉以配之，使為前鋒。

translations.literal: He therefore feasted Laozhi publicly, hailed him elder brother before the crowd, assigned elite weapons entirely to him, and made him vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong publicly adopted Laozhi as “elder brother” and armed him fully.

sentences.zh: 行至竹裏，牢之背恭歸朝廷。

translations.literal: Marching to Zhuli Laozhi betrayed Gong for the court.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuli Laozhi defected to court.

sentences.zh: 恭既死，遂代恭為都督兗、青、冀、幽、并、徐、揚州、晉陵軍事。

translations.literal: After Gong died Laozhi succeeded Gong as area commander over Yan Qing Ji You Bing Xu Yang and Jinling military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi inherited Wang Gong’s mega-command after his death.

sentences.zh: 牢之本自小將，一朝據恭位，眾情不悅，乃樹用腹心徐謙之等以自強。

translations.literal: Laozhi began as petty officer—seizing Gong’s seat overnight displeased everyone—therefore he planted trusted men like Xu Qianzhi to bolster himself.
translations.idiomatic: A jumped-up captain commanding peers—Laozhi stuffed posts with cronies.

sentences.zh: 時楊佺期、桓玄將兵上表理王恭，求誅牢之。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Quanqi and Huan Xuan marched memorializing Wang Gong’s grievance demanding Laozhi’s death.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Quanqi and Huan Xuan demanded Liu Laozhi’s head for Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 牢之率北府之眾馳赴京師，次於新亭。

translations.literal: Laozhi led Beifu masses racing to capital halting at Xin Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi rushed Beifu troops to Xin Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 玄等受詔退兵，牢之還鎮京口。

translations.literal: Xuan and others received edict to withdraw troops—Laozhi returned to Jingkou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Edict recalled coalition—Laozhi went back to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 及孫恩攻陷會稽，牢之遣將桓寶率師救三吳，復遣子敬宣為寶後繼。

translations.literal: When Sun En seized Kuaiji Laozhi sent general Huan Bao to relieve three Wu circuits and dispatched son Jingxuan as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Against Sun En Laozhi sent Huan Bao with Jingxuan trailing.

sentences.zh: 比至曲阿，吳郡內史桓謙已棄郡走，牢之乃率眾東討，拜表輒行。

translations.literal: By reaching Qu’a Interior Minister of Wu Commandery Huan Qian had fled—Laozhi led hosts east campaigning memorializing without awaiting reply.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Qu’a he found Huan Qian gone—marched east on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 至吳，與衛將軍謝琰擊賊，屢勝，殺傷甚眾，徑臨浙江。

translations.literal: At Wu he joined General Who Guards the Court Xie Yan beating rebels repeatedly with heavy casualties pressing Zhe River.
translations.idiomatic: With Xie Yan he smashed Sun En toward Zhe River.

sentences.zh: 進拜前將軍、都督吳郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: Advanced General Who Leads the Van and commander of Wu military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted vanguard general commanding Wu theater.

sentences.zh: 時謝琰屯烏程，遣司馬高素助牢之。

translations.literal: At that time Xie Yan camped Wucheng sending marshal Gao Su to aid Laozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan at Wucheng lent Gao Su.

sentences.zh: 牢之率眾軍濟浙江，恩懼，逃於海。

translations.literal: Laozhi crossed Zhe River with massed armies—En fled seaward.
translations.idiomatic: Mass crossing scared Sun En back to sea.

sentences.zh: 牢之還鎮，恩復入會稽，害謝琰。

translations.literal: Laozhi returned to garrison—En re-entered Kuaiji killing Xie Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi withdrew—Sun En killed Xie Yan retaking Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 牢之進號鎮北將軍、都督會稽五郡，率眾東征，屯上虞，分軍戍諸縣。

translations.literal: Laozhi advanced title General Who Guards the North commanding five Kuaiji commanderies—east campaign camped Shangyu dividing troops among counties.
translations.idiomatic: Made northern guard general over five Kuaiji counties—headquartered Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 恩復攻破吳國，殺內史袁山松。

translations.literal: En again smashed Wu interior killing Interior Minister Yuan Shansong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En seized Wu circuit killing Yuan Shansong.

sentences.zh: 牢之使參軍劉裕討之，恩復入海。

translations.literal: Laozhi sent aide Liu Yu against him—En fled sea again.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu drove Sun En seaward again.

sentences.zh: 頃之。

translations.literal: Before long.
translations.idiomatic: Soon.

sentences.zh: 恩浮海奄至京口，戰士十萬，樓船千餘。

translations.literal: En sailed sea appearing at Jingkio—hundred thousand warriors—over thousand tower ships.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En landed at Jingkou with a hundred thousand men and thousand war junks.

sentences.zh: 牢之在山陰，使劉裕自海鹽赴難，牢之率大眾而還。

translations.literal: Laozhi was at Shanyin—sent Liu Yu from Haiyan toward relief—himself led main host back.
translations.idiomatic: From Shanyin he rushed Liu Yu from Haiyan while retracing main army.

sentences.zh: 裕兵不滿千人，與賊戰，破之。

translations.literal: Yu’s troops numbered under one thousand yet defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Under one thousand men Liu Yu still won.

sentences.zh: 恩聞牢之已還京口，乃走鬱洲，又為敬宣、劉裕等所破。

translations.literal: En hearing Laozhi returned Jingkou fled to Yuzhou—again smashed by Jingxuan and Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En fled Yuzhou—again crushed by Jingxuan and Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 及恩死，牢之威名轉振。

translations.literal: After En died Laozhi’s awe-name swelled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En’s death magnified Laozhi’s fame.

sentences.zh: 元興初，朝廷將討桓玄，以牢之為前鋒都督、征西將軍，領江州事。

translations.literal: Early Yuanxing court planned Huan Xuan’s purge naming Laozhi vanguard commander General Who Conquers the West managing Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing opened with Laozhi slated western conqueror and Jiangzhou chief striking Xuan.

sentences.zh: 元顯遣使以討玄事諮牢之。

translations.literal: Yuanxian sent envoys consulting Laozhi on attacking Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian consulted Liu Laozhi’s strategy.

sentences.zh: 牢之以玄少有雄名，杖全楚之眾，懼不能制，又慮平玄之後功蓋天下，必不為元顯所容，深懷疑貳，不得已率北府文武屯洌洲。

translations.literal: Laozhi judged Xuan’s young fame mighty commanding all Chu—feared inability to control—also feared surpassing all merit after victory—certain Yuanxian could not abide—deeply doubtful—reluctantly led Beifu civil and martial ranks camping Lie Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Xuan’s Chu army and post-victory purge Laozhi stalled at Lie Isle torn.

sentences.zh: 桓玄遣何穆說牢之曰：「自古亂世君臣相信者有燕昭樂毅、玄德孔明，然皆勳業未卒而二主早世，設使功成事遂，未保二臣之禍也。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan sent He Mu telling Laozhi: “Since antiquity chaotic ages rarely sustain ruler-minister trust—Yan Zhao had Le Yi and Liu Bei had Kongming yet both sovereigns died mid-task—even completed merit seldom spared ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He Mu cited tragic fate of Le Yi and Zhuge Liang—merit invites slaughter.

sentences.zh: 鄙語有之：'高鳥盡，良弓藏；

translations.literal: Proverb says: When high birds vanish good bows hide;
translations.idiomatic: “When birds are gone bows get stashed;

sentences.zh: 狡兔殫，獵犬烹。

translations.literal: when crafty rabbits die hunting dogs boil.”
translations.idiomatic: when rabbits die dogs boil.”

sentences.zh: '故文種誅於句踐，韓白戮于秦漢。

translations.literal: Hence Wen Zhong died under Goujian Han Xin Bai Qi fell in Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhong died for Goujian—Han Xin likewise.

sentences.zh: 彼皆英雄霸王之主，猶不敢信其功臣，況凶愚凡庸之流乎！

translations.literal: Those heroic overlords still doubted meritorious servants—how more vulgar dolts!
translations.idiomatic: Even wise kings killed heroes—how trust petty court?

sentences.zh: 自開闢以來，戴震主之威，挾不賞之功，以見容於暗世者而誰？

translations.literal: Since creation who wielded awe shaking sovereign while boasting unbeatable merit survived dark ages?
translations.idiomatic: Who holding conqueror’s awe survives jealous throne?

sentences.zh: 至如管仲相齊，雍齒侯漢，則往往有之，況君見與無射鉤屢逼之仇邪！

translations.literal: Only cases like Guan Zhong serving Qi or Yong Chi ennobled under Han occur—how more you bear arrow-shaft grudge with lord!
translations.idiomatic: Rare exceptions like Guan Zhong—you suffer arrow-feud history with Yuanxian!

sentences.zh: 今君戰敗則傾宗，戰勝亦覆族，欲以安歸乎？

translations.literal: Now defeat wipes your clan victory likewise uproots you—where seek peace?
translations.idiomatic: Lose—clan dies; win—still extinguished.

sentences.zh: 孰若翻然改圖，保其富貴，則身與金石等固，名與天壤無窮，孰與頭足異處，身名俱滅，為天下笑哉！

translations.literal: Better suddenly shift plan preserving fortune—body firm as metal fame endless—versus severed corpse erased name mocked world!
translations.idiomatic: Switch sides—live famed—or lose head laughingstock!

sentences.zh: 惟君圖之。

translations.literal: Consider carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Choose wisely.

sentences.zh: 」牢之自謂握強兵，才能算略足以經綸江表，時譙王尚之已敗，人情轉沮，乃頗納穆說，遣使與玄交通。

translations.literal: Laozhi deemed himself holding strong troops genius enough to rule south—Prince Shang already defeated morale sank—partially accepted Mu—sent envoys treating with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking Lie Isle leverage plus Shang’s defeat Laozhi flirted with Xuan.

sentences.zh: 其甥何無忌與劉裕固諫之，並不從。

translations.literal: Nephew He Wuji with Liu Yu urgently remonstrated—ignored.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji and Liu Yu pleaded vainly.

sentences.zh: 俄令敬宣降玄。

translations.literal: Soon ordered Jingxuan surrender Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jingxuan defect to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄大喜，與敬宣置酒宴集，陰謀誅之，陳法書畫圖與敬宣共觀，以安悅其志。

translations.literal: Xuan rejoiced feasting Jingxuan plotting secretly to kill him—displayed law calligraphy paintings studying together to soothe him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wined Jingxuan plotting murder—shared scrolls to lull him.

sentences.zh: 敬宣不之覺，玄佐吏莫不相視而笑。

translations.literal: Jingxuan noticed nothing—Xuan’s aides exchanged smiles.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan blind—staff smirked.

sentences.zh: 元顯既敗，玄以牢之為征東將軍、會稽太守，牢之乃歎曰：「始爾，便奪我兵，禍將至矣！

translations.literal: After Yuanxian fell Xuan named Laozhi eastern conqueror Kuaiji prefect—Laozhi sighed: “Barely begun already stripped of troops—disaster nears!”
translations.idiomatic: Post-Yuanxian Xuan made Laozhi Kuaiji governor—Laozhi groaned losing troops instantly.

sentences.zh: 」時玄屯相府，敬宣勸牢之襲玄，猶豫不決，移屯班瀆，將北奔廣陵相高雅之，欲據江北以距玄，集眾大議。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan camped minister’s mansion—Jingxheng urged Laozhi raid Xuan—Laozhi hesitated moved camp Bandu meant fleeing north to Prefect Gao Yazhi of Guangling plotting Jiangbei resistance calling council.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuan occupied minister mansion Jingxuan urged strike—Laozhi wavered shifted Bandu planning flight to Gao Yazhi—called war council.

sentences.zh: 參軍劉襲曰：「事不可者莫大於反，而將軍往年反王兗州，近日反司馬郎君，今復欲反桓公。

translations.literal: Army adviser Liu Xi said: “Nothing exceeds rebellion in unacceptability—yet general you rebelled against Wang Inspector of Yanzhou in former years, lately rebelled against Minister Sima’s son, now again wish to rebel against Duke Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi warned: “Nothing tops treason—yet you betrayed Wang Gong, then Sima Yuanxian, now mean to betray Huan Xuan.”

sentences.zh: 一人而三反，豈得立也。

translations.literal: One man rebelling thrice—how can he stand!”
translations.idiomatic: Three betrayals—how stand?”

sentences.zh: 」語畢，趨出，佐吏多散走。

translations.literal: Speech finished he hurried out; adjutants largely scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed off—staff fled.

sentences.zh: 而敬宣先還京口拔其家，失期不到。

translations.literal: Yet Jingxuan had earlier returned to Jingkou pulling his household—missed the rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan preemptively evacuated Jingkou—never arrived.

sentences.zh: 牢之謂其為劉襲所殺，乃自縊而死。

translations.literal: Laozhi assumed Xi killed him and therefore hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking murder Laozhi hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 俄而敬宣至，不遑哭，奔于高雅之。

translations.literal: Presently Jingxuan arrived—no time to mourn—fled to Gao Yazhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan came too late—ran to Gao Yazhi.

sentences.zh: 將吏共殯斂牢之，喪歸丹徒。

translations.literal: Officers together encoffined Laozhi—funeral returned to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Officers buried him—sent body to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 桓玄令斫棺斬首，暴屍於市，及劉裕建義，追理牢之，乃復本官。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan ordered coffin split head cut corpse exposed in market—when Liu Yi raised righteous army Laozhi was posthumously cleared—restored original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan desecrated corpse—Liu Yi later rehabilitated Laozhi.

sentences.zh: 敬宣，牢之長子也。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was Laozhi’s eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan was eldest son.

sentences.zh: 智略不及父，而技藝過之。

translations.literal: His strategy fell short of his father yet martial arts surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Less cunning than Laozhi—better with arms.

sentences.zh: 孫恩之亂，隨父征討，所向有功。

translations.literal: During Sun En’s turmoil he followed father campaigning—everywhere meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against Sun En with distinction.

sentences.zh: 為元顯從事中郎，又為桓玄諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He served Yuanxian as attendant gentleman-in-chief and Xuan as adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yuanxian then Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 牢之敗，與廣陵相高雅之俱奔慕容超，夢丸土而服之，既覺，喜曰：「丸者桓也，丸既吞矣，我當復土也。

translations.literal: After Laozhi’s defeat he fled with Administrator of Guangling Gao Yazhi to Murong Chao—dreaming he swallowed clay pills—awakening joyful said: “Pills mean Huan—pill swallowed—I shall recover soil.”
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing to Murong Chao he dreamed swallowing earth—omen of reclaiming land from Huan.

sentences.zh: 」旬日而玄敗，遂與司馬休之還京師。

translations.literal: Within ten days Xuan fell—thereupon with Sima Xiuzhi returned capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Xuan fell—returned with Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 拜輔國將軍、晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Appointed General Who Supports the State and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Named supporting-state general and Jinling prefect.

sentences.zh: 與諸葛長民破桓歆於芍陂，遷建威將軍、江州刺史，鎮尋陽。

translations.literal: With Zhuge Changmin he crushed Huan Xin at Shaopi—rose General Who Establishes Might and Jiangzhou Inspector garrisoning Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Beat Huan Xin at Shaopi—became Jiangzhou inspector at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 又擊桓亮、苻宏於湘中，所在有功。

translations.literal: Further attacked Huan Liang and Fu Hong in Xiang region—merit everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Crushed Huan Liang and Fu Hong in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 安帝反政，徵拜冠軍將軍、宣城內史，領襄城太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor An resumed rule summoned him champion general interior minister of Xuancheng concurrent governor of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An recalled him as champion general Xuancheng prefect.

sentences.zh: 譙縱反，以敬宣督征蜀軍事、假節，與甯朔將軍臧喜西伐。

translations.literal: When Qiao Zong rebelled Jingxuan commanded western Shu expedition with credential staff campaigning west with General Who Calms the North Zang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Against Qiao Zong he led Shu expedition with Zang Xi.

sentences.zh: 敬宣人自白帝，所攻皆克。

translations.literal: Jingxuan entered from Baidicheng—every assault succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: From Baidi every siege prevailed.

sentences.zh: 軍次黃獸，與偽將譙道福相持六十餘日，遇癘疫，又以食盡，班師，為有司所劾，免官。

translations.literal: Army halted at Huangshou—stalemated rebel general Qiao Daofu sixty days—plague struck plus grain exhausted—withdrawal court impeached—stripped office.
translations.idiomatic: Stalled at Huangshou sixty days—plague and famine—retreat cost office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為中軍諮議，加冠軍將軍，尋遷鎮蠻護軍、安豐太守、梁國內史。

translations.literal: Before long served central army adviser plus champion general soon transferred barbarian protector Administrator of Anfeng interior minister of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Later adviser champion general barbarian protector.

sentences.zh: 會盧循反，以冠軍將軍從大軍南討。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun rebelled went champion general following main army south.
translations.idiomatic: Joined southern campaign against Lu Xun as champion.

sentences.zh: 循平，遷左衛將軍、散騎常侍，又遷征虜將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: After Xun pacified rose Left Guard general gentleman at palace gate then General Who Conquers the Caitiffs Qingzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Lu Xun became left guard then Qingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 尋改鎮冀州，為其參軍司馬道賜所害。

translations.literal: Soon reassigned Ji Province killed by staff aide Sima Daosi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province posting ended—staff aide Sima Daosi murdered him.

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪

translations.literal: Yin Zhongkan
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪，陳郡人也。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongkan was a native of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan hailed from Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖融，太常、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Ancestor Rong served Chamberlain for Ceremonial and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yin Rong headed ritual office and personnel.

sentences.zh: 父師，驃騎諮議參軍、晉陵太守、沙陽男。

translations.literal: Father Shi served adviser on chariot-and-cavalry staff Administrator of Jinling village baron of Shaying.
translations.idiomatic: Father Yin Shi was cavalry adviser Jinling prefect Shaying baron.

sentences.zh: 仲堪能清言，善屬文，每雲三日不讀《道德論》，便覺舌本間強。

translations.literal: Zhongkan could discourse pure talk and compose—often said if three days pass without reading the “Dao-de Discourse” his tongue root stiffens.
translations.idiomatic: Famed qingtan stylist—claimed skipping three days of 《Dao-de Discourse》 numbed his tongue.

sentences.zh: 其談理與韓康伯齊名，士咸愛慕之。

translations.literal: His reasoning matched Han Kangbo’s fame—gentlemen adored him.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked with Han Kangbo in philosophical debate.

sentences.zh: 調補佐著作郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to editorial aide.
translations.idiomatic: Became editorial aide.

sentences.zh: 冠軍謝玄鎮京口，請為參軍。

translations.literal: Champion Xie Xuan garrisoned Jingkou requesting him as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan wanted him on staff at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 除尚書郎，不拜。

translations.literal: Appointed gentleman of Masters of Writing—declined.
translations.idiomatic: Offered secretariat post—refused.

sentences.zh: 玄以為長史，厚任遇之。

translations.literal: Xuan made him chief clerk with heavy favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan kept him as chief clerk with trust.

sentences.zh: 仲堪致書于玄曰：

translations.literal: Zhongkan wrote Xuan:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Xie Xuan:

sentences.zh: 胡亡之後，中原子女鬻于江東者不可勝數，骨肉星離，荼毒終年，怨苦之氣，感傷和理，誠喪亂之常，足以懲戒，復非王澤廣潤，愛育蒼生之意也。

translations.literal: After Hu tribes fell Central Plain sons and daughters sold east of Yangzi count beyond measure—kin scattered like stars suffering poison year round—resentful vapor wounds harmonious principle—truly chaos’s routine enough for warning—yet not kingly moisture nurturing common folk.
translations.idiomatic: After northern collapse captives flooded Jiangdong—he pleaded humane resettlement policy.

sentences.zh: 當世大人既慨然經略，將以救其塗炭，而使理至於此，良可歎息！

translations.literal: Present great men aspire to strategy meant to rescue them from fire yet governance reaches this—deeply sigh-worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Leaders claim rescue yet policies still brutal—lamentable!

sentences.zh: 願節下弘之以道德，運之以神明，隱心以及物，垂理以禁暴，使足踐晉境者必無懷戚之心，枯槁之類莫不同漸天潤，仁義與干戈並運，德心與功業俱隆，實所期於明德也。

translations.literal: May you, sir, enlarge them with dao, move them with spirit, extend heart to things, hang principle to restrain violence—so whoever treads Jin soil harbors no sorrow—withered folk alike receive heavenly moisture—benevolence marches with arms virtuous mind rises with merit—this bright virtue’s hope.
translations.idiomatic: He urged benevolent occupation merging force with virtue.

sentences.zh: 頃聞抄掠所得，多皆采梠饑人，壯者欲以救子，少者志在存親，行者傾筐以顧念，居者籲嗟以待延。

translations.literal: Lately hearing spoils seized mostly stalk-grain starving folk—strong wish save children young aim preserve parents—travelers empty baskets longing stayers sigh awaiting delay.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders seize starving families torn apart—heartrending.

sentences.zh: 而一旦幽縶，生離死絕，求之於情，可傷之甚。

translations.literal: Yet suddenly imprisoned alive separated dead seeking feeling—deeply wounding.
translations.idiomatic: Captivity splits families cruelly.

sentences.zh: 昔孟孫獵而得麑，使秦西以之歸，其母隨而悲鳴，不忍而放之，孟孫赦其罪以傅其子。

translations.literal: Formerly Mengsun hunted capturing fawn sent Qin Xi ride home—its mother followed crying—unable endure released—Mengsun pardoned keeper tutoring son.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun’s deer parable urged mercy.

sentences.zh: 禽獸猶不可離，況於人乎！

translations.literal: Birds and beasts may not be torn from kin—how much more humans!
translations.idiomatic: Beasts cling to young—humans worse!

translations.idiomatic: Eight thousand glittering troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 既至，仲堪唯以飯餉其軍。

translations.literal: Once arrived Zhongkan only fed army rice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan served only rice.

sentences.zh: 佺期大怒曰：「今茲敗矣！

translations.literal: Quanqi greatly angry said: “Now this defeat!”
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi roared defeat certain.

sentences.zh: 」乃不見仲堪。

translations.literal: Therefore refused see Zhongkan.
translations.idiomatic: Snubbed Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 時玄在零口，佺期與兄廣擊玄。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan at Lingkou Quanqi elder brother Guang assault Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi brothers struck Xuan at Lingkou.

sentences.zh: 玄畏佺期之銳，乃渡軍馬頭。

translations.literal: Xuan feared Quanqi sharpness crossed army Matou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan fled to Matou fearing Quanqi.

sentences.zh: 明日，佺期率殷道護等精銳萬人乘艦出戰，玄距之，不得進。

translations.literal: Next day Quanqi led Yin Daohu crack ten thousand aboard ships battle Xuan resisted unable advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand elite stalled against Xuan.

sentences.zh: 佺期乃率其麾下數十艦，直濟江，徑向玄船。

translations.literal: Quanqi therefore led dozens ships straight ford aimed Xuan fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi rammed Xuan ships.

sentences.zh: 俄而回擊郭銓，殆獲銓，會玄諸軍至，佺期退走，餘眾盡沒，單馬奔襄陽。

translations.literal: Soon turning attacked Guo Quan nearly captured Quan Xuan reinforcements arrived Quanqi retreated remainder drowned lone horse fled Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Raid turned—Guo Quan saved—Quanqi routed solo flight.

sentences.zh: 玄追軍至，佺期與兄廣俱死之，傳首京都，梟於朱雀門。

translations.literal: Xuan pursuit arrived Quanqi elder brother Guang both died transmitted heads capital exposed Zhuque Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers killed heads hung Zhuque.

sentences.zh: 弟思平，從弟尚保、孜敬，俱逃於蠻。

translations.literal: Younger brother Siping cousins Shangbao Zijing fled barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Kin fled tribes.

sentences.zh: 劉裕起義，始歸國，歷位州郡。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu raised the righteous army they began returning to allegiance to Jin and subsequently served in successive prefectural posts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu’s victory brought them back into Jin service in successive local posts.

sentences.zh: 孜敬為人剽銳，果於行事。

translations.literal: Zijing nature rash fierce decisive action.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing rash warrior.

sentences.zh: 昔與佺期勸殷仲堪殺殷顗，仲堪不從，孜敬拔刃而起，欲自己出取之，仲堪苦禁乃止。

translations.literal: Formerly with Quanqi urged Yin Zhongkan kill Yin Yi Zhongkan refused Zijing drew blade rose wished seize personally Zhongkan bitterly forbade stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing nearly murdered Yin Yi—stopped.

sentences.zh: 及為梁州刺史，常怏怏不滿其志。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou Inspector always resentful unsatisfied ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter Liang post.

sentences.zh: 經襄陽，見魯宗之侍衛皆佺期之舊也，孜敬愈憤，見於辭色。

translations.literal: Passing Xiangyang seeing Lu Zongzhi guards all Quanqi old troops Zijing angrier showed face.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Lu guards sparked rage.

sentences.zh: 宗之參軍劉千期於座面折之，因大發怒，抽劍刺千期立死。

translations.literal: Zongzhi aide Liu Qianqi seat rebuked therefore great anger drew sword stabbed Qianqi instant death.
translations.idiomatic: Killed Liu Qianqi in temper.

sentences.zh: 宗之表而斬之。

translations.literal: Zongzhi memorial executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu executed Zijing.

sentences.zh: 思平、尚保後亦以罪誅，楊氏遂滅。

translations.literal: Siping Shangbao later also executed crime Yang clan extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining kin executed—clan ended.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians’ appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historians’ commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：生靈道斷，忠貞路絕，棄彼弊冠，崇茲新履。

translations.literal: Historian says: living way severed loyalty paths cast aside abandoning worn caps honoring new shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Age abandoned loyalty for novelty.

sentences.zh: 牢之事非其主，抑亦不臣，功多見疑，勢陵難信，而投兵散地，二三之甚。

translations.literal: Laozhi served wrong lord likewise disloyal merit abundant suspected power bullying hard trust casting weapons scattered ground wavering extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi betrayed repeatedly—trust shattered.

sentences.zh: 若夫司牧居愆，方隅作戾，口順勤王，心乖抗節。

translations.literal: If shepherd errs frontier rebels mouth claims aiding king heart resists mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Warlords mouth loyalty rebel secretly.

sentences.zh: 王恭鯁言時政，有昔賢之風。

translations.literal: Wang Gong upright speech policy possessed ancient worthy wind.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong spoke truth like ancients.

sentences.zh: 國寶就誅，而晉陽猶起。

translations.literal: Guobao executed yet Jinyang still rose.
translations.idiomatic: Executing Guobao failed to stop revolt.

sentences.zh: 是以仲堪僥倖，佺期無狀，雅志多隙，佳兵不和，足以亡身，不足以靜亂也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhongkan gambled Quanqi lawless aspirations gaps many fine weapons discord enough destroy self insufficient pacify turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan and Quanqi schemed lawlessly—arms divided—destroyed selves not chaos.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孝伯懷功，牢之總戎。

translations.literal: Encomium: Xiaobo cherished merit Laozhi commanded armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong sought glory Laozhi led hosts.

sentences.zh: 王因起釁，劉亦慚忠。

translations.literal: Wang sparked strife Liu also ashamed loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang stirred trouble Liu betrayed honor.

sentences.zh: 殷楊乃武，抽旆爭雄。

translations.literal: Yin Yang martial lowered banners contending.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yang warriors clashed banners.

sentences.zh: 庾君含怨，交鬥其中。

translations.literal: Yu Kai harbored hatred battling midst.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai nursed grudge amid fray.

sentences.zh: 猗歟群采，道睽心異。

translations.literal: Ah splendid talents dao diverged hearts differed.
translations.idiomatic: Talents split paths.

sentences.zh: 是曰亂階，非關臣事。

translations.literal: Thus chaos stairs—not ministers’ affair alone.
translations.idiomatic: Order collapsed—fault not ministers alone.
